chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Dexter Gordon joins Armstrong; the "Grooving" session
summary: The 1944 Decca sides come up; Dexter joined in California for about a month during wartime travel.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: BEGINNING OF TAPE 9

Back with Teddy McRae. This is Cassette No. 9. You were with Louie and you -- The band, when you were with it, made a few recordings which apparently were never issued until "Grooving" was issued on this Decca Lp, "Louis Armstrong Rare Items, 1935 to 1944," from Decca jazz heritage series. This is DE9225. And "Grooving" is that orchestra recorded in August 9, 1944. I was a couple of months old at that time. Jess Brown, Thomas Gritter, Fats Ford, Lester Curran, were the trumpet sections. And you were in the reed section with Dexter Gordon. So you met up with Dexter one more time. And --
Yeah. Dexter joined us in California.
Okay. So in other words, Dexter joined Louie Armstrong after you joined Louie

Armstrong -- after you became musical director.
Yeah.
You chose Dexter.
Dexter worked the California area. Something happened. We needed a tenor player --
They (Inaudible) recorded in LA.
Yeah. (Inaudible).
Dexter just joined the band for about, oh, I'd say about a month. I don't think he stayed with us long, because he wanted to leave.

(Inaudible), you know -- he wasn't with us too long. Because we were playing these -- Remember, those were the war days, you know -- '44 and '45 -- second world war. And we were travelling in buses and anything we could get our hands on to move around.

And the Army and Navy was moving us around in planes. Like we were in California, we'd go out to the airport and fly out to Tucson, Arizona and do a benefit for the, you know, for the Army. Then come back and do something for the Navy, or something
